elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Section 3.4: "Customer may terminate this Agreement (including all Service Option Attachments) or any Service Option Attachment ... for convenience at the end of any calendar month". Service Option Attachments are the attachments referenced in Order Forms, so both agreement-level and order-level exits exist; the carve-out for prerequisite attachments narrows but does not remove the right. (Note: the deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present: false" is a false negative — the operative text plainly contains the grant.)

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: The clause requires "at least one month's prior written notice" and permits termination only "at the end of any calendar month", so the effective notice can exceed 30 days (a one-month notice given mid-month runs to the following month-end). To hit the preferred element the drafter would need "thirty (30) days' prior written notice" without the calendar-month effectiveness anchor.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: No refund language anywhere in the rendered clause; Section 3.4 addresses only notice and early termination charges. A pro-rata refund of prepaid charges for the post-termination period would have to be inserted. The finding expressly declines to press this.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: IBM's only exits in the cited text are the 90-day non-renewal election tied to "the end of the then-current term" (a RENEWAL mechanic, not mid-term T4C) and breach termination; no mid-term Vendor convenience right is granted or added.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Customer's right runs on "at least one month's prior written notice", which is shorter and therefore more favourable to Customer than the 60–90 day fallback window; the fallback notice requirement is satisfied a fortiori.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Operation adds to 3.4(b): "paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments, capped at three (3) months' charges." The cap is unconditional and attaches to the only fee mechanic in the convenience clause.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: The auto-renewal provision ties IBM's election to terminate to notice "at least ninety (90) days prior to the end of the then-current term", with the Service Option Attachment simply not renewing at term end; no mid-term Vendor convenience right exists, so the term-end limitation is satisfied.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: "at least ninety (90) days prior to the end of the then-current term" — the only Vendor no-cause exit requires 90 days' notice; the element is also satisfied vacuously because IBM has no mid-term convenience right.

reasons: Position-complete at the fallback: all four fallback elements are met after the edit, so the redline is sufficient as drafted. Preferred is not reached (no pro-rata refund of prepaid charges; notice is "one month" effective at calendar month-end rather than 30 days), which the rationale correctly acknowledges rather than claims.

The deterministic signal "Customer convenience termination present: false" is a mechanical false negative — the rendered Section 3.4 expressly grants Customer a convenience right; the substantive gap was only the uncapped early termination charges in 3.4(b), which the operation fixes.

Minimality holds: the single insertion is ", capped at three (3) months' charges" in 3.4(b). No other words were deleted or paraphrased, the favourable one-month notice and the prerequisite-attachment structure are retained, and no extras (survival tails, refund mechanics, procedures) were added.

Intent is preserved: the auto-renewal/non-renewal mechanic, breach termination, notice timing and the Attachment A / Service Option Attachment cross-references all survive; the cap qualifies an existing charge without creating an undefined term ('charges' is the contract's own fee vocabulary) or a dangling reference.

If the team later wants the preferred position, the operative repairs are (i) replace "at least one month's prior written notice" and the "end of any calendar month" anchor with "thirty (30) (days') prior written notice", and (ii) add "IBM will refund prepaid charges for the period after the effective date of termination on a pro-rata basis."
